about: Every INSERT … ON CONFLICT (<target>) on main when tooling/ci/conflict-keys.mjs landed (18 Nov 2026) that leaves another unique key of its table unabsorbed, one entry per insert and key, with its verdict: safe and why, or a race with its bug issue. Read from the code by four reviewers and spot-checked; races are not yet reproduced. The list only shrinks: fix a race, then remove its entry. New code takes the fix the check prints, never a new entry here.

entries.why: insertMembership locks the crew row `FOR UPDATE` and re-checks the (crew,user) membership before inserting (blueprint-service.ts:490-505), so a duplicate of this row returns early. All callers run SERIALIZABLE with maxAttempts 5 retrying 40001 (blueprint-service.ts:259, :589; packages/db/src/connection.ts) after reading crew_members by user_id, so a concurrent placement of the same user elsewhere surfaces as a retried serialization failure; a user already in another crew via joinCrew is a different, real conflict (note: that 23505 is not mapped to a typed error).

crewId is deterministic, but name is checked (`SELECT ... WHERE name=$base AND season`, blueprint-service.ts:534-537) inside a SERIALIZABLE transaction retried on 40001 (:259, :589); two concurrent crews deriving one name turn into a serialization failure (the key was read first) and the retry picks the suffixed name. A duplicate of the same crewId writes the same name and is retried the same way.

participation_key is `campaign:join:<campaignId>:<accountId>` (campaigns.ts:613), so it is 1:1 with (campaign_id, account_id). For non-competition campaigns only `FOR SHARE` on the campaign row is held (campaigns.ts:1750), which does not serialise; two Join presses at once both pass the existence checks (1744, 1753) and the loser can raise 23505 participations_one_per_account instead of getting the winner's row. Competition joins are safe (advisory lock at 1776 plus re-check).

Same-issue duplicates are serialised by pg_advisory_xact_lock on the code hash (campaigns.ts:1510), but the loser then finds the winner's row by code_hash (campaigns.ts:1512) and throws campaigns.voucher_code_taken instead of returning it, though the docstring (campaigns.ts:1499) promises the same issue returns the stored voucher; the ON CONFLICT (issue_key) never fires. Also the batch writer (watch.ts:593) inserts code_hash without that lock, so an issue racing a batch on the same code gets raw 23505 vouchers_code_hash_uq (nothing maps it).

chain_tx is not in the insert's column list (reward-payer.ts:201), so it is NULL and NULLs never clash on reward_payments_chain_tx_key; also serialised by FOR UPDATE on reward_intents (reward-payer.ts:197).
Batch rows set code to NULL (watch.ts:578) and vouchers_code_uq is a plain UNIQUE (20261029140018_vouchers.sql:19), so NULLs never clash.
issue_key is `voucher:batch:<batchId>:<n>` with batchId fresh `cbt_${randomUUID()}` (watch.ts:569, 580); a repeat of the same batch reference returns early under the advisory lock (watch.ts:564-567).
id is fresh `vch_${randomUUID()}` per row (watch.ts:576); a repeat batch is stopped before insert by the advisory lock on the batch reference and the re-read (watch.ts:564-567).

Same-user writers are serialised by `SELECT … FROM users WHERE id = … FOR UPDATE` (phone-change.ts:83); a phone clash is a different user holding that number, and the caller catches 23505 and maps it to invalidCode (phone-change.ts:114-120).

This insert writes state 'verify_only' (auth-key-ring.ts:173), so the partial index WHERE state='active' never applies; all writers also hold pg_advisory_xact_lock('identity.auth_signing_keys') (auth-key-ring.ts:167).

No duplicate-absorption race: same-user calls are serialised by `users … FOR UPDATE` (signin-methods.ts:115 via readUser at 378). A phone clash means two different users linking one number at once; both pass the pre-check (signin-methods.ts:383) and the loser gets raw 23505 signin_phones_phone_key, which nothing maps to identity.method_taken (signin-methods-router.ts:65-97): a correct refusal with the wrong error shape, worth a catch-by-name fix but not a lost duplicate.

applyBlock takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(schema:indexer.projection:<chain>) before any read (postgres-store.ts:617), and the unwind paths take the same lock (:787, :807), so all writers of blocks are serialised. A second canonical block at a height is a real competing-block conflict the comment at :699-702 intends the index to refuse.

window_id and epoch are both caller-supplied in the share batch body (submit-share.ts:268-270, :333-350); persistShares inserts with no lock before it (window-store.ts:83-93). Two share batches for the same new window with an epoch (concurrent miners, or a client retry) both insert; the loser raises 23505 windows_epoch_asset_uidx, not caught anywhere in src (no 23505 handling), instead of the DO UPDATE path.
gateway_id is randomUUID() generated per request at relay.ts:138, so a duplicate of this row never shares it.
This insert writes no approval_id (postmortems.pg.ts:43-45), so it is NULL; the column is a plain UNIQUE (drizzle/0031_notify_status_postmortems.sql:14), which allows many NULLs.

id = inboxId(name, version) (compliance/router.ts:168), derived from the target columns. The `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` at store.ts:271 locks nothing when the row does not exist yet, so two concurrent defines of the same name+version both insert; the loser raises 23505 compliance_inboxes_pkey instead of reaching the 'racing define' branch the comment at store.ts:281 expects.

upsertSourceMapping takes a single global pg_advisory_xact_lock('ops.crm.source-mapping-writes') (crm.ts:706) and checks source_key collisions with another id (crm.ts:714-715) before inserting; it is the only writer of crm_source_mappings.
Same exclusive 'ops.crm.privacy' lock and pre-read by canonical_contact_id (restore-privacy.ts:173, :187-205): any other row on this contact throws restore_tombstone_conflict before the insert.

applyErasureArchive holds the exclusive pg_advisory_xact_lock('ops.crm.privacy') (restore-privacy.ts:173), which excludes the normal writers' shared lock (privacy.ts:33), and pre-reads rows by id OR canonical_contact_id OR request_id, throwing restore_tombstone_conflict on any mismatch (restore-privacy.ts:187-205). A clash then is a corrupted archive, refused by name.

Under the exclusive 'ops.crm.privacy' lock (restore-privacy.ts:173); notification request_ids are randomUUID() per row at creation (privacy.ts:330), so a restored value belongs only to its own (intent, submission), which is pre-read at :220-222.

idempotency_key is the client's key (restore/desk.ts:191), repeated on retry. start() checks `WHERE idempotency_key` then inserts with no lock (run-store.ts:144-153); two overlapping retries both pass the check and both insert, and the loser raises 23505 restore_runs_idempotency_key_key (it is a non-arbiter index, so this happens whether or not restore_no also clashes) instead of returning the stored run.

Same pattern: the client's idempotency key (desk.ts:232, :280) is checked then inserted with no lock (run-store.ts:177-186); two overlapping retries of one step both insert and the loser raises 23505 restore_steps_idempotency_key_key instead of returning the stored step.
token_hash is the hash of a fresh randomBytes(24) token (p2p-service.ts:2879-2882), so it differs on every call, retry included.

contract_deal_id is not in the insert's column list (p2p-service.ts:3526-3542), so it is NULL and the partial index WHERE contract_deal_id IS NOT NULL never applies; it is set later by UPDATE (p2p-service.ts:3804).
address is not written (custody/service.ts:266-267), so it is NULL and custody_wallets_address_uq (WHERE address IS NOT NULL, 0104_pay_custody_accounts.sql:63) never applies.

A clash on (source, payment_ref) is caught: the 23505 handler re-reads by source and ref and returns the winner (review-queue-store.ts:245-249); the id is also derived from the same ref (heldCaseId, review-queue-store.ts:254).
Two enqueues with the same payment ref clash on (source, payment_ref); the 23505 handler adopts the winner's case by ref, or re-reads by id (review-queue-store.ts:356-363).

is_default is not in the insert (defaults false, 0088_pay_destination_default_invoice_lines.sql:19) and the DO UPDATE does not set it (merchant-payout-destination.ts:359-370), so the partial index WHERE is_default never applies.
is_default is not in the insert (defaults false) and the DO UPDATE does not set it (merchant-payout-destination.ts:385-396), so the partial index WHERE is_default never applies.
id is fresh newId() from randomBytes(16) on every call (merchant-webhooks.ts:249-251, 955).
release_spent_for is not in the insert or the DO UPDATE SET (screening/store.ts:91-99), so the partial index WHERE release_spent_for IS NOT NULL never applies to rows this writes.

idempotency_key is derived from (subscriptionId, occurrence) (charge-cycle.ts:118), the same as the target, but the only insert into this table (subscription-service.ts:1245) runs after `SELECT … FROM pay.subscriptions WHERE id = … FOR UPDATE` (subscription-service.ts:1225-1231), which serialises every writer for that subscription.
ledger_tx_id is not in the insert's column list (subscription-service.ts:1245-1251), so it is NULL and the partial index never applies.
payment_id is not in the insert's column list (subscription-service.ts:1245-1251), so it is NULL and the partial index never applies.

quote_ref is non-null only on a first claim that goes through acceptQuoteForSend, which locks the quote row FOR UPDATE (send-out/door.ts:166-171) and refuses a second client_ref on it with withdrawal_quote.already_used (door.ts:191-195). A same-client_ref retry gets 'mine' and is absorbed by the target.

Same-withdrawal duplicates are serialised by `SELECT … FROM pay.withdrawals WHERE id = … FOR UPDATE` (returns/service.ts:84). A return_ref clash is two different withdrawals given one rail ref at once; the loser gets raw 23505 withdrawal_returns_ref_uq instead of withdrawal_return.ref_differs (the pre-check at 101-105 is not under a lock covering both): a correct refusal with the wrong error shape, not a lost duplicate.
id is randomUUID() generated in the call (library/postgres-repository.ts:296), new on every insert.
id is randomUUID() generated in the call (library/postgres-repository.ts:172), new on every insert.
id is randomUUID() generated in the call (notify/postgres-repository.ts:79), new on every insert.
id is randomUUID() generated in the call (team/postgres-repository.ts:199), new on every insert.
This insert writes no ticket_id (chat.ts:513-517), so it is NULL; chat_sessions_ticket_uq is a plain UNIQUE (drizzle/20261107080000_support_chat.sql:38) that allows many NULLs.

configure() takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('svc-support'), hashtext('surveys')) (survey-settings.ts:175), the only writer of surveys, and deactivates every other active survey (:210) before inserting active=true.

The upsert never writes client_convert_id (column list at convert/quote-store.ts:236-243), so the new row is NULL and outside the partial index (WHERE client_convert_id IS NOT NULL). That column is set only later by an UPDATE (convert/convert-history.ts:343).

reserve_key is copy.reserve:<followId> (copy/follows.ts:59), a one-to-one function of follow_id. An equal follow_id always means an equal reserve_key, which the arbiter absorbs. A different follow_id never clashes on follow_id.
id is a fresh randomUUID() on every call, inline in the INSERT … SELECT (futures/conditional-orders/service.ts:1588).
id is a fresh randomUUID() (futures/conditional-orders/service.ts:1509) and trigger_key is book:<id> (service.ts:247-248), so trigger_key is unique on every call.
trigger_key is not in the column list (service.ts:1572-1574), so it is NULL, and NULLs do not clash in a plain unique index. syncRiskStop writes armed rows only.
liquidation_rung_id is not written by this reduce-only insert (matched-orders.ts:1505-1509), so it is NULL.

Runs in the transaction that first takes SELECT … FOR UPDATE on the open position row (matched-orders.ts:1411-1415), so two retries of one reduce serialise, and the second sees the committed row in the arbiter pre-check.
The MM seed row writes no client_order_id (index.ts:1230 column list), so it is NULL. orders_client_id_idx is a plain unique index (drizzle/0000_trade_init.sql:145) where NULLs never clash.
evidence_kind is 'TRANSITION' (market-lifecycle.ts:797), and the partial index covers only evidence_kind = 'AUTHORITY_DOSSIER' (drizzle/0035_market_lifecycle_publications.sql:26-28).
evidence_kind is 'CORRECTION' and market_id is NULL (market-lifecycle.ts:810), outside the AUTHORITY_DOSSIER partial index.
evidence_kind is 'TRANSITION' (market-lifecycle.ts:797), and the partial index covers only 'AUTHORITY_DOSSIER' (drizzle/0035:29-31).
evidence_kind is 'CORRECTION' (market-lifecycle.ts:810), outside the AUTHORITY_DOSSIER partial index.

reconciliation_key is non-NULL only for OUTCOME_UNKNOWN/PARTIAL (market-lifecycle.ts:789-792). The only production caller, admin/market-mode.ts:206-209, always writes outcome APPLIED, so the key is NULL.
appendCorrection writes reconciliation_key NULL (market-lifecycle.ts:810).

Rows inserted as open/expired never enter the partial index (lifecycle IN ('bound','settled')). saveBound/saveSettled reach it only via DO UPDATE on the existing quote row, so a retry of the same quote updates its own row. A 23505 there comes only from a different sibling quote of the same RFQ, which is a real second accept that must refuse, and saveBound maps it with refuseSecondAccept (otc/quote-store.ts:271-277).

fills.ts:340-354 catches 23505 around this insert and then reads by (market_id, sequence, liquidity) and compares the money columns (fills.ts:363-375). A redelivery is absorbed; a sequence reuse by a different match is refused, which is the mapped real conflict.
The house MM stub row writes no client_order_id (fills.ts:524-532), so it is NULL, and NULLs never clash in the plain index (0000_trade_init.sql:145).
